http.title: HTTP & hosters
http.description: Direct HTTP, DDownload cookies and the Premiumize API key share the same isolated client identity; signed components stay installable.

capture.title: Capture agent
capture.description: Clipboard, Click'n'Load, NZB file association and Windows hotfolders use the native agent.

usenet.title: Usenet
usenet.description: Server priorities and encrypted credentials are configurable; yEnc and safe post-processing building blocks are built in.

facts.web_ui_configured: Configured port · applied on next start

pairing.title: Pair native agent
pairing.description: The bearer secret is shown only once. Only its SHA-256 digest with the {scope} scope is persisted.
pairing.copy_hint: Copy now – it cannot be retrieved later
pairing.copied_description: The full command is in your clipboard.
pairing.extension_hint: Browser extension: use the raw token below in the extension options.
pairing.extension_steps: In the extension options set the server URL to {origin} and paste this token, then press “Test connection”. See extension/README.md for installation.
pairing.token_copied_description: The capture token is in your clipboard.
pairing.label: Connection name
pairing.queue_control_help: Allows “Pause all” and “Resume all” in the agent's tray menu – nothing more. Without it the agent only hands links in.

revoke.title: Remove capture connection
revoke.description: The agent “{label}” immediately loses access to LinkGrabber and NZB import.

export.title: Export settings
export.description: Download all server-side settings, categories, accounts and integrations as a versioned JSON bundle.
export.include_secrets_description: Credentials and cookies are protected with the passphrase and never written as plaintext.
export.passphrase_short: Use a passphrase with at least 8 characters.

import.title: Import settings
import.description: Restore or migrate a version 1 rDownloader settings bundle.
import.invalid_file: The selected file is not a valid rDownloader settings bundle.
import.passphrase_required: Enter the passphrase used to create this backup.
import.confirm_description: All settings, categories, accounts, proxies, Usenet servers, hotfolders and stream channels will be replaced. Pause active downloads first. Capture-agent hotfolders imported on another installation must be paired again.
import.password_hint: Replacing the configuration asks for the password again.

full.title: Scheduled encrypted full backup
full.description: Writes the database, the queue, the LinkGrabber, torrent sessions, plugin trust and credentials, encrypted, to your destinations – while downloads keep running. Downloaded files are not included.

key.title: Passphrase
key.missing: No passphrase set up yet. Without one no full backup is written.
key.hint: The passphrase is stored nowhere, only the key derived from it, in the secret store. A restore asks for it again. A new passphrase applies to future backups; older ones still open with the old one.
key.short: The passphrase needs at least {min} characters.
key.current_required: Enter the current passphrase to replace it.

schedule.title: Schedule
schedule.enabled_description: Runs in the background. A failure stops no download and lands in the history.
schedule.cron_description: Five fields: minute hour day month weekday, e.g. 0 3 * * * for every day at 3:00.
schedule.verify_description: Checks the newest archive at every destination: fetched back, compared and opened. Empty is off.
schedule.no_destination: No active destination yet – add one below before you switch the schedule on.

destinations.title: Destinations
destinations.description: Every destination gets its own copy. One that is unreachable is tried again and costs only its own entry in the history.
destinations.empty: No destination yet. Add a folder, an object storage bucket or an rclone remote.
destinations.deleted: Destination removed. Its archives stay where they are.
destinations.name: Name
destinations.name_description: Optional; without one the list shows the address.
destinations.path_description: Absolute path on the machine running rDownloader; a mounted NAS share works too.
destinations.profile_none: No profile yet – add one in the object storage settings first.
destinations.prefix_description: <bucket>/<folder>; without a bucket the profile's own bucket is used.
destinations.remote_description: name:path of a remote configured in rclone – WebDAV, SFTP, cloud drives and more.
destinations.keep_last_description: Number of archives; empty keeps all.
destinations.keep_days_description: Younger archives stay; empty keeps all.

retention.hint: The newest archive always stays. Only archives this installation wrote there are ever removed – never anybody else's files.
retention.result: Keeps {keep}, removes {remove} – nothing is deleted yet.

destinations.verify_none: There is no archive there yet.
destinations.stored_key: checked with the stored key, not the passphrase

passphrase_check.title: Verify with passphrase
passphrase_check.description: “Verify newest” uses the key kept for the schedule. A restore asks only for the passphrase, and a lost passphrase cannot be recovered. This opens the newest archive with the passphrase.
passphrase_check.hint: The archive is read in full; nothing is written.

history.title: History
history.empty: No full backup has run yet.

full_restore.title: Restore a full backup
full_restore.description: Opens an archive with its passphrase, shows what it holds, checks it in a throwaway copy and switches to it at the next start. The running installation stays startable until the restored one has started once.

status.staged: The restore of {archive} ({date}) is waiting. Restart rDownloader to switch to it; the current state is kept until the restored one has started once.
status.switching: A start is switching to {archive} right now.
status.failed: The restore of {archive} did not start on {date}; the previous installation was kept. Reason: {reason}

dialog.title: Restore a full backup
dialog.description: Pick the archive, enter its passphrase, check its contents, map the storage roots, test – only then confirm.

source.title: Archive
source.no_runs: No successful backup in the history.

passphrase.label: Passphrase of this backup
passphrase.hint: Asked for every time: the key kept for the schedule is never used for a restore.

preview.title: Contents
preview.newer: A newer version made this backup. Update to at least that version first ({version} runs here).
preview.counts: {categories} categories, {accounts} accounts, {proxies} proxies, {servers} Usenet servers, {subscriptions} subscriptions, {hotfolders} hot folders

mapping.title: Storage roots
mapping.hint: Where each storage root lies on this machine. Leave a field empty to keep the path. Paths from another system (drive letters, shares) need a folder here; every path below moves with it and can never leave it.

test.ok: The test restore found nothing that stops the restore.
test.failed: The test restore found errors that stop the restore.
test.summary: {packages} packages, {moved} paths moved, {credentials} credentials restored, {migrated} migrations applied.

confirm.label: I understand: at the next start this backup replaces the whole installation. The current state is kept until the restored one has started once.
confirm.staged: Restore staged. Restart rDownloader to switch to it.

password.label: Administrator password
password.hint: The restore replaces the password, passkeys and tokens at the next start, so it asks for the password again.

mcp.title: API access & MCP
mcp.description: API tokens authenticate REST, the CLI, SABnzbd- and qBittorrent-compatible clients, and the MCP server at {endpoint}. Selectable areas replace blanket {scope} access; only the SHA-256 digest is persisted.
mcp.copy_hint: This API token is shown only once – store it safely in the intended client now.
mcp.token_hint: Raw token for clients that expect only the API key.
mcp.command_copied: The claude mcp add command is in your clipboard.
mcp.token_copied: The API token is in your clipboard.
mcp.header_hint: Clients that read the header from an environment variable (ChatGPT desktop): enter this complete value.
mcp.header_copied: The Authorization header is in your clipboard.
mcp.single_source_hint: Configure only one source for the Authorization header. If two are sent, only the first counts — a correct token in second place is never read.

revoke.title: Revoke API token
revoke.description: The client “{label}” immediately loses its API and MCP access.

edit.label: Change permissions
edit.hint: The token value stays the same: the client keeps working and reaches the new areas from its next request onwards. Removing everything is not possible here — revoke the token for that.
edit.empty: Choose at least one area, or revoke the token.

read.name: Read
read.description: Queue, progress, packages and system status. Grants nothing that changes anything.

intake.name: Add links
intake.description: Adding links, files and containers to the LinkGrabber. What a *arr instance or a browser extension needs.

queue.name: Control the queue
queue.description: Start, pause, retry, reorder and delete queued work.

config.name: Configuration
config.description: Categories, rules, schedules and service settings that carry no credential.

secrets.name: Stored credentials
secrets.description: Hoster accounts, proxy profiles, Usenet servers and the settings export. Nothing else grants this.

admin.name: Administration
admin.description: Plugins, service switches, updates and backups. Does not include stored credentials.

metrics.name: Metrics
metrics.description: Only the Prometheus route /api/v1/metrics. Reaches nothing else, not the queue and not MCP.

mcp.scopes_hint: Grant only what the client actually needs. Anything that acts can also read, so reading does not have to be added separately.
mcp.sensitive_warning: This token will be able to read stored credentials or administer the service. Nothing else grants either, so give it only to a client that genuinely needs it.

readiness.title: Is the setup finished?
readiness.complete: Everything the setup asks for is in place.
readiness.outstanding: One step is still open. | {count} steps are still open.

login.label: Administrator login
login.done: Set, or deliberately switched off for a trusted network.
login.missing: No password is set yet and the login is not switched off.

storage.label: Storage destination
storage.done: At least one destination is configured.
storage.missing: Downloads have nowhere to go until a destination exists.
storage.ephemeral: A destination is configured, but at least one is not on persistent storage.

category.label: Category
category.missing: Without a category nothing can be sorted into a folder.

wizard.label: Setup finished
wizard.missing: The setup was never finished; run it again from the sidebar.

sessions.title: Signed-in devices
sessions.description: Every open sign-in to this installation. If something here is not yours, end it and change the password.

revoke.title: End this session?
revoke.description_current: You will be signed out on this device and will have to sign in again.

revoke_others.title: Sign out everywhere else?
revoke_others.description: {count} other sessions will be ended. This one stays signed in.

proxy.title: Reverse proxy
proxy.description: If a proxy sits in front, rDownloader has to know about it. Otherwise every request counts as coming from the proxy, and the session cookie may not match the scheme the browser is actually using.
proxy.external_url_hint: Scheme, host and sub-path in one setting, so they cannot disagree. Leave empty when there is no proxy.
proxy.trusted_hint: One address or CIDR range per line. A forwarded client address is believed only from these; everything else counts as the caller itself.
proxy.cookie_hint: “Automatic” follows the scheme of the external URL and is right almost always.
proxy.warning_no_proxies: An external URL is set but no trusted proxy is. Every request will then look as though it came from the proxy: rate limiting and the session list show one address for everybody.
proxy.warning_no_url: Trusted proxies are set but no external URL is. The cookie then cannot be marked Secure automatically.
proxy.allowed_hosts_hint: One name per line that you open the service by in a browser, such as nas.lan. IP addresses, localhost and the external URL's host always work; any other name is refused, so no foreign page gets in through DNS rebinding.
proxy.login_off_title: Sign-in is off although a proxy or an external address is set
proxy.login_off_description: Without sign-in, every request from this machine that carries no forwarding header counts as the administrator. A local tunnel or proxy that sets no X-Forwarded-For makes everyone behind it the administrator. Switch sign-in back on under General, or make sure your proxy sets the header.

mfa.title: Two-factor sign-in
mfa.description: Optional. After the password, a code from an authenticator app is also required. The recovery codes are the only other way back in — there is nobody here to prove your identity to.

enrol.once: Visible only now. None of this can be retrieved once you leave the page.
enrol.scan: Scan this code with your authenticator app:
enrol.recovery: Recovery codes — keep these somewhere safe:
enrol.qr_alt: QR code for setting up the authenticator app
enrol.manual: Or enter the key by hand:

remove.title: Remove this second factor?
remove.description: “{label}” will no longer be able to answer a challenge.

regenerate.title: Issue new codes?
regenerate.description: The recovery codes you have now will stop working.

disable.hint: Switching it off takes the password, not a code. A lost device must not be final.

step_up.label: Password
step_up.hint: Adding, removing or switching off a factor asks for the password again.

passkeys.title: Passkeys
passkeys.description: Sign in with your device instead of your password. Your authenticator checks a PIN or a fingerprint before it will sign, so one step covers both. The password keeps working — a passkey is another way in, not a replacement.
passkeys.unsupported: This browser cannot use passkeys here. They need a secure connection: either https, or reaching the service at localhost.
passkeys.failed: The passkey could not be set up.
passkeys.name_hint: So you know which device this is when you come to remove it.

remove.title: Remove this passkey?
remove.description: “{label}” will stop being able to sign in. Your password still works.

passkeys.step_up_hint: Adding or removing a passkey asks for the password again.

password.title: Administrator password
password.description: Replaces the password you sign in with. You need the current one for it. There is no recovery without the current password.
password.mismatch: The two new passwords do not match.
password.sessions_hint: The change ends every session. This window stays signed in; every other device has to sign in again.
password.tokens_hint: API tokens keep working, because they do not hang off the password. Anyone who knew the old one could have issued themselves some, though: check the token list.

logs.title: Clear the service log?
logs.description: {count} log records will be removed for good. The audit log and the statistics stay, as do downloads, packages and settings.

audit.title: Clear the audit log?
audit.description: {count} audit records will be removed for good. The clearing itself becomes the first entry in the emptied log. The service log and the statistics stay, as do downloads, packages and settings.

stats.title: Clear the transfer statistics?
stats.description: {count} statistics rows will be removed for good, the all-time totals among them. The service log and the audit log stay, as do downloads, packages and settings.

notifications.title: Clear the notification history?
notifications.description: {count} finished deliveries will be removed from the history for good. Deliveries still queued or retrying stay, as do destinations, rules, the service log, the audit log and the statistics.

notifications_pending.title: Discard the pending notifications?
notifications_pending.description: {count} notifications still queued or retrying will be deleted and never sent. Delivered and failed deliveries stay in the history, as do destinations, rules, the service log, the audit log and the statistics.

storage_operations.title: Clear the storage history?
storage_operations.description: {count} completed, failed and interrupted moves and duplicate links will be removed from the history for good. An operation still running stays. No file is moved or deleted, and an interrupted move is still carried on at the next start.

content_index.title: Clear the content index?
content_index.description: {count} index entries will be removed. Files and downloads stay untouched, but until a file is indexed again it is not recognised as a content duplicate and cannot be the original of a duplicate link. “Check the content index” (also run at every start) re-indexes finished downloads still in the queue whose SHA-256 is known and whose file is still in place. Files of removed or never hashed downloads come back only when downloaded again.

history.title: Clear the download history?
history.description: {count} entries will be removed from the download history for good. The download list, the files, the statistics and the logs stay untouched.

session_limits.title: How long a sign-in lasts
session_limits.description: A sign-in ends when it has not been used for this long or reaches its maximum lifetime, whichever comes first. A shorter setting ends older sign-ins at once.
session_limits.idle_description: Hours without a request before you have to sign in again. 1 to 720 (30 days).
session_limits.max_description: Hours from signing in after which it ends, even in the middle of work. 1 to 2160 (90 days).

extension.connected_description: A browser extension has just reported in. Accounts that take over your browser's sign-in receive the session through it.
extension.missing_title: No browser extension has reported in yet
extension.missing_description: Checked every few seconds; once the extension is paired and reports in, it shows here.
extension.why: Hoster accounts that take over your browser's sign-in — DDownload, for example — need the rDownloader browser extension: only it can hand the session over from the browser. Pairing is optional; without the extension, a username and password or an API key remain.
extension.step_install: Install the rDownloader extension in the browser you are signed in to the hoster with.
extension.step_pair: Press “Pair” below: rDownloader shows a token once — copy it.
extension.step_options: In the extension options enter {origin} as the server URL, paste the token, press “Test connection”, then “Save”.
extension.modal_description: The sign-in at the hoster comes from your browser, and only the extension can hand it over. Pair it here without leaving the page.

updates.title: Updates
updates.description: rDownloader reads a signed list of releases from GitHub and tells you when a new version is out. Nothing is installed without you.
updates.enabled_description: Fetches a public, signed file only and sends nothing about this installation.
updates.channel_description: Stable gets releases only, Beta also gets pre-releases (vX.Y.Z-beta.N).
updates.channel_forced_stable: Your package manager publishes no betas, so this installation reads the stable channel.
updates.not_configured: This build carries no update key; the update check is off.

modal.title: rDownloader {version}
modal.download_hint: Replace the program files of this installation with the new version; your settings and downloads stay where they are.
modal.command_hint: {kind} manages this installation. Update it with:
modal.install_hint: rDownloader downloads the new version unless it is already downloaded, backs up its database, stops, replaces its program files and starts again. Your settings and downloads stay where they are.
modal.rollback_automatic: If the new version does not start properly, the previous one comes back by itself.
modal.rollback_unavailable: This update through the Windows installer cannot be taken back by itself: the installer of the running version was not kept. From the next update on it can.

hints.docker_recreate: Then recreate the container, e.g. with docker compose up -d.
hints.deb_file: The repository carries releases only. A beta, or a package installed from a download, is installed from the file: sudo apt install ./<file>.deb
hints.rpm_file: The repository carries releases only. A beta, or a package installed from a download, is installed from the file: sudo dnf install ./<file>.rpm

install.confirm_description: rDownloader stops for about a minute and starts again as {version}. Running downloads are saved and continue afterwards. This page reconnects by itself.
install.reconnecting: rDownloader is restarting – waiting for it to answer …
install.lost: rDownloader has not answered for minutes. End it if it still runs and start it by hand; if the update was left incomplete, the previous version comes back at that start.
install.reload_hint: Reload the page to use the new version’s interface.

state.preparing: Writing the backup before the update …
state.rolling_back: {version} does not start properly; bringing back {from} …
state.rolled_back: {version} did not start properly, so {from} runs again.

download.ready: {version} is downloaded and verified; “Install and restart” uses this file.

agents.outdated_description: A capture agent still runs version {agent}, rDownloader already runs {service}. From 1.8.1 on, the agent restarts itself within a minute of an update. If it does not — because it is older, or another user started it — quit it from its tray icon or in Task Manager and start it again; on Linux, systemctl --user restart rdownloader-capture does both.
agents.self_offered: A capture agent installed without rDownloader offers itself version {version}: choose “Install update to {version}” in its tray menu, or run rdownloader-capture update.

oidc.title: Sign in through an identity provider
oidc.description: Sign in with the account you already use at Authentik, Authelia, Keycloak or Pocket ID (OpenID Connect). There is still one administrator: the one account you link here.
oidc.redirect_uri: Redirect URI – register it at the provider
oidc.external_url_missing: Without an external URL there is no redirect URI. Set it under Security → Reverse proxy.
oidc.link_hint: Linking opens the provider; the account you sign in with there becomes the administrator.

unlink.title: Unlink this account?
unlink.description: Nobody signs in through the provider afterwards until you link an account again.

remove.title: Remove the identity provider?
remove.description: The configuration, the client secret and the linked account are deleted.

oidc.password_is_off: Signing in with the password is switched off
oidc.password_is_off_hint: Only the machine the service runs on brings it back: {command}. Passkeys keep working, and the password still confirms changes.

password_off.ready: This session came from the provider: you can switch the password sign-in off.
password_off.needs_provider_session: Sign in through the provider once; only from that session can the password sign-in be switched off.
password_off.title: Switch the password sign-in off?
password_off.description: Afterwards you sign in through the provider or with a passkey. The way back is only on the machine the service runs on: {command}

oidc.issuer_hint: Exactly as the provider states it – with or without the trailing slash.
oidc.client_secret_kept: Leave empty to keep the stored one.
oidc.display_name_hint: For example Authentik or Pocket ID.
oidc.group_hint: Optional: the linked account must also be in this group.
oidc.provider_logout: Sign out at the provider too
oidc.provider_logout_hint: Off: signing out ends only the session here, your other services stay signed in.
oidc.step_up_hint: Every change here asks for the password again.

token_expiry.label: Expires
token_expiry.hint: An expired token is refused like a revoked one and stays in the list until you revoke it.

token_rate.label: Calls per minute
token_rate.hint: REST and MCP together. Empty means no limit; a call above it is refused until the minute is over.
